To express the number in Cartesian form, we expand the parentheses and substitute the values of the cosine and sine.

First, we find $\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{11\pi }{6})$ and $\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{11\pi }{6}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{11\pi }{6}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,,\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{11\pi }{6}) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute the values and expand the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =14(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{11\pi }{6})+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{11\pi }{6})) \\  & =14(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\text{i}\,\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{14\sqrt{3}}{2}-\text{i}\,\frac{14}{2} \\  & =7\sqrt{3}-7\,\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$
